scope: Checkpoint format/admission only; sanitizer supported-input is separate.

CP-A.title: Retain v1 checkpoint semantics
CP-A.user_impact: Oversized results remain unsupported through this path and may fail before publication.
CP-A.compatibility: Keep v1 read compatibility, restore types, files normalization, ordering, independent decoded lists, and full raw JSON admission at 64,000,000 bytes.
CP-A.resource_security: Preserve encryption/HMAC/digest, scope/tenant, expiry, cancellation, atomicity, spill and recovery safeguards.
remaining_evidence: Cancellation/exhaustion, database/broker, tenant concurrency and publication
CP-A.assessment: Least disruptive technically; does not solve observed failure and requires owner decision.

CP-B.title: Authorize formal checkpoint-format policy investigation
CP-B.authorization_scope: Investigation only; no implementation, migration, deployment, changed limit, or qualification.
CP-B.user_impact: May inform future behavior; no support promise before policy and acceptance evidence.
CP-B.compatibility: Versioned format, v1 reads, rollout plan, persisted-checkpoint compatibility, migration and rollback analysis.
CP-B.resource_security: Define aggregate logical and encrypted-storage budgets separately; prove memory/disk/CPU/time bounds and retain all existing crypto, tenant, integrity, expiry, cancellation, atomicity and recovery guarantees.
CP-B.assessment: Candidate has unresolved restore/quota differences; result unavailable; evidence does not justify adoption.
